_comment: Confusable Pairs boss round. Rapid forced choice between two specific principle ids per question ('option_a' vs 'option_b'). 'correct_principle' must equal one of them. Deliberately mixes Error Prevention/Error Recovery and User Control and Freedom/Flexibility and Efficiency of Use, in varied option order so students can't just memorise a position.

questions.scenario: As you type a new password, a live checklist ticks off 'at least 8 characters' and 'one number' before you submit the form.

feedback.correct: Right - the mistake is caught before it happens.
feedback.incorrect: This checklist appears before you submit, catching the mistake before it happens - that's Error Prevention, not Error Recovery.

questions.scenario: After you submit a form with a missing field, a red message appears next to the empty box saying 'Email address is required'.

feedback.correct: Right - this message appears after the mistake was made, helping the user fix it.
feedback.incorrect: This message only appears after the form was submitted with a mistake already made - that's Error Recovery, not Error Prevention.

questions.scenario: A clearly visible 'Undo' link appears for a few seconds after you archive an email, letting you bring it straight back.

feedback.correct: Right - Undo is an escape route out of an action you didn't mean to take.
feedback.incorrect: This gives you a way to reverse a mistake you already made - that's User Control and Freedom, an emergency exit, not a shortcut for experts.

questions.scenario: Experienced spreadsheet users can press Ctrl+Shift+L to instantly apply filters, while new users can still use the toolbar button.

feedback.correct: Right - a shortcut that speeds up an expert user without removing the option for beginners.
feedback.incorrect: This is a shortcut that speeds up an experienced user - that's Flexibility and Efficiency of Use, not an escape route out of a mistake.

questions.scenario: Before a shared document is permanently deleted, a confirmation dialog asks 'Are you sure? This can't be undone' with Cancel highlighted.

feedback.correct: Right - the confirmation stops the deletion before it happens.
feedback.incorrect: This dialog appears before anything is deleted, stopping the mistake before it happens - that's Error Prevention.

questions.scenario: When a file upload fails, the app explains 'File too large - please choose a file under 10MB' and offers a 'try again' button.

feedback.correct: Right - this explains what already went wrong and how to fix it.
feedback.incorrect: The upload has already failed by the time this message appears - that's Error Recovery, helping the user recognise and fix the mistake.

questions.scenario: A multi-step signup wizard has a visible 'Cancel and exit' option on every screen, so users are never trapped in the process.

feedback.correct: Right - an always-available exit out of a process is User Control and Freedom.
feedback.incorrect: This is about never being trapped in a process - an emergency exit - that's User Control and Freedom, not a speed shortcut for experts.

questions.scenario: Power users can save a custom keyboard macro to repeat a common multi-step action in a single keystroke.

feedback.correct: Right - a macro that speeds up a repeated task for an experienced user is Flexibility and Efficiency of Use.
feedback.incorrect: This lets an experienced user work faster on a task they already know - that's Flexibility and Efficiency of Use, not an escape route.
